tb-405-1.question:
Which of the following actions can cause the long solenoid above to give a stronger magnetic field inside the solenoid?

(1) Insert a copper core into the solenoid.

(2) Compress the solenoid.

(3) Stretch the solenoid.

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1) and (3) only
tb-405-1.reasoning:
Copper is a non-magnetic material and does not affect the strength of the magnetic field.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

By B = μ0nI, the field strength can be raised by increasing the number of turns per unit length.

∴ (2) is correct. (3) is incorrect.

tb-405-2.question:
Two electromagnets are placed as shown below (Fig b). X and Y are identical solenoids.

Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) Y produces a stronger magnetic field than X.

(2) The magnetic force exerted on X by Y is stronger than the magnetic force exerted on Y by X.

(3) X and Y attract each other.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-405-2.reasoning:
A larger current produces a stronger magnetic field.

∴ (1) is correct.

The magnetic force exerted on X by Y and the magnetic force exerted on Y by X form an action-and reaction pair. They are equal in magnitude.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

The end of X facing Y is an N-pole and the end of Y facing X is an S-pole.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-405-6.question:
A bar magnet is placed on a weighing scale, and an electromagnet is right above it (Fig e). Which of the following actions will increase the reading of the scale?

A Move the electromagnet slightly downwards.

B Take away the aluminium core.

C Reduce the resistance of the variable resistor.

D Halve the number of turns per unit length of the coil.
tb-405-6.reasoning:
The bottom end of the electromagnet behaves like an S-pole and applies an upward attractive force on the bar magnet. To increase the scale reading, the magnetic force should be reduced.

Moving the electromagnet downwards will increase the magnetic force.

∴ A is incorrect.

Taking away the aluminium core will not affect the magnetic force.

∴ B is incorrect.

Reducing the resistance of the variable resistor will increase the magnetic force.

∴ C is incorrect.

Halving the number of turns per unit length of the coil will reduce the magnetic force.

∴ D is correct.

tb-405-8.question:
P, Q, R and S are four parallel long straight wires located at the corners of a regular hexagon (Fig g). All wires carry the same magnitude of current in the directions shown. O is the centre of the hexagon. Should the current in which wire be reversed so that the resultant magnetic field at O become zero?

A P only

B Q only

C R only

D None of the above.
tb-405-8.reasoning:
At point O, the magnetic field produced by Q and R cancelled out each other.

To make the resultant magnetic field zero, the magnetic field produced by P and S must cancel each other. This can be achieved by reversing the current in P.

If the current in Q is reversed, the resultant magnetic field would point upwards.

If the current in R is reversed, the resultant magnetic field would point to the right.

tb-405-9.question:
P and Q are two parallel long straight wires (Fig h). The current I in Q flows downwards. Point X is 2d from P and d from Q. If the resultant magnetic field at X is zero, what are the magnitude and direction of the current in P?

A I2(upwards)

B I2(downwards)

C 2I(upwards)

D 2I(downwards)
tb-405-9.reasoning:
By right-hand grip rule, wire Q produces a magnetic field pointing into the page at point X. Therefore, wire P must produce a magnetic field pointing out of the page at point X so that the resultant magnetic field is zero. By right-hand grip rule, the current in P points downwards.

μ0IP2πrP =μ0IQ2πrQ

μ0IP2π(2d) =μ0I2πd

IP = 2I

tb-405-10.question:
P, Q, R, S, T and U are six parallel long straight wires located at the corners of a regular hexagon (Fig i). All wires carry the same magnitude of current in the directions shown. What is the direction of the resultant magnetic field at the centre O of the hexagon?

A Upwards

B Downwards

C To the left

D To the right
tb-405-10.reasoning:
At point O, the magnetic field produced by U and R cancel out each other.

By symmetry, the resultant magnetic field produced by P and T points upwards and the resultant magnetic field produced by Q and S also points upwards.

Therefore, the resultant magnetic field by the six wires at point O points upwards.

tb-405-19.question:
Figure q shows the schematic diagram of a doorbell. The rod PQ is made of a soft-iron rod and a plastic rod joined together. A spring is attached to the end P of the rod.

Fig q

(a) Briefly explain how a ‘ding-dong’ sound is heard when the bell-push is pressed and released. (3 marks)

(b) Explain whether the doorbell can still work if each of the following changes is made.

(i) The polarity of the battery is reversed.

(ii) The soft-iron rod is replaced with a copper rod.

(iii) The coil is made of thicker wires. (6 marks)
tb-405-19.answer:
(a) When the bell-push is pressed, a current flows through the coil. The coil produces a magnetic field which attracts the soft-iron rod. 1A

The soft iron rod is pulled into the coil and the tip Q hits metal plate A. This produces the ‘ding’ sound. 1A

When the bell-push is released, no current flows through the coil and the soft-iron rod is no longer attracted. The spring pushes the soft iron rod out of the coil and the tip P hits metal plate B. This produces the ‘dong’ sound. 1A

(b) (i) The bell still works. 1A

Reversing the polarity of the battery reverses the direction of the magnetic field produced by the coil. The soft iron rod is still attracted into the coil. 1A

(ii) The bell does not work. 1A

The copper rod is not magnetic and is not attracted into the coil when a current flows through the coil. 1A

(iii) The bell still works. 1A

The total resistance of the circuit decreases if the coil is made of thicker wires.

This increases the current the current through the coil and hence makes the electromagnet stronger. 1A
